dimensions.name: PREMISE_MATURITY
dimensions.description: Core story problem should feel substantively suitable for a 12-year-old, not like preschool play dressed in harder vocabulary.

dimensions.name: NARRATIVE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support layered goals, changing information, reversals, and multi-step progression while remaining readable.

dimensions.name: CONCEPTUAL_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Allow systems, evidence, competing explanations, responsibility, trust, and consequences without requiring adult-only abstraction.

dimensions.name: CAUSAL_DEPTH
dimensions.description: Important outcomes should follow from multiple linked causes rather than one-step problem-solution patterns.

dimensions.name: INFERENCE_DEMAND
dimensions.description: Reader should sometimes connect clues, motives, patterns, or consequences without every relationship being stated directly.

dimensions.name: AGENCY_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Character should face meaningful options, trade-offs, strategy, or uncertainty; choices must not be predetermined.

dimensions.name: STAKES_CONSEQUENCE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Actions should matter to reputation, relationships, access, goals, safety, or world state without requiring graphic danger.

dimensions.name: SOCIAL_RELATIONSHIP_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support trust, disagreement, rivalry, mentorship, competing interests, and mixed motives without adult melodrama.

dimensions.name: PREDICTABILITY_CHALLENGE
dimensions.description: Avoid obvious one-beat resolutions; allow wrong hypotheses, reversals, incomplete information, and earned payoff.

dimensions.name: WONDER_DISCOVERY
dimensions.description: Adventure-oriented episodes should offer places, systems, discoveries, mysteries, or experiences larger than ordinary daily-life simulation.

dimensions.name: LANGUAGE_READABILITY
dimensions.description: Use clear, natural language suitable for an independent 12-year-old reader. Story maturity must not depend on jargon.

required_story_capabilities: Meaningful protagonist role in the world
At least one non-trivial objective or unresolved question
Meaningful discovery or change in understanding
A real choice, strategic constraint, or consequential action
Persistent consequence or reusable world-state value
Adventure-oriented modes should include wonder, exploration, mystery, or extraordinary experience
reject_signals: Core premise is primarily pretend-play with toys, chores, or ordinary-room simulation unless explicitly requested
Difficult vocabulary is doing the work of making an otherwise young-child premise appear older
Problem resolves through one obvious attempt with no meaningful complication
Character mostly observes while adults or the world solve the important problem
Episode can be summarized as collect clue A, clue B, clue C with no reasoning change
Stakes are cosmetic and no persistent consequence can result
Mystery is solved before the character earns the relevant evidence
World can be swapped for any generic setting without changing the premise materially
language_rules: Technical terms are allowed when they serve the world or reasoning and can be understood in context
Do not infantilize dialogue or narration
Do not use vocabulary difficulty as a substitute for premise maturity
Keep exposition bounded and reveal information through action, observation, dialogue, or consequence where practical
safety_rules: Adventure tension is allowed without requiring graphic violence
Fear, danger, loss, rivalry, and uncertainty may be present when developmentally appropriate
Do not assume maturity requires darker or more violent content
Do not force romance, grief, betrayal, or trauma merely to make a story feel older
calibration_notes: A strong age-12 premise may involve systems failing, competing hypotheses, expedition planning, social disagreement, hidden history, evidence testing, or strategic risk.
A simple premise may still pass when deliberately selected for a calm/intimate mode, but should not be used as the default adventure ceiling.
Evaluate premise, narrative, conceptual, interest, and language maturity independently.

character.name: Deniz
character.origin_summary: Deniz grew up in Meridian Harbor apprenticing under a demanding mapmaker, driven to prove that patient observation can reveal what official charts miss.
character.current_role: apprentice cartographer under supervised but increasingly independent fieldwork

identity_anchors.statement: Deniz believes careful observation matters more than authority or bravado.
Deniz wants recognition earned through proof, not granted by rank.

core_drives.drive: Prove that rigorous observation reveals truths official maps miss.
Earn the right to chart beyond the home strait.

internal_tensions.side_b: pull toward reckless pursuit of a personally meaningful mystery
internal_tensions.description: Deniz's discipline is tested whenever a discovery brushes close to personal stakes.

immediate_desires: earn the right to chart beyond the home strait
find hard evidence others cannot dismiss
immediate_avoidances: being dismissed as a reckless or overconfident child surveyor

world.era: age of sail with precision mechanical navigation
world.habitat: a vast island chain divided by deep channels, storm belts and partially mapped outer seas
world.technology_level: sailing ships, mechanical clocks, optical instruments, printing presses and hand-built navigation devices
world.magic_level: rare, rule-bound geophysical phenomena associated with tides, magnetic stone and ancient infrastructure; no arbitrary spellcasting
world.summary: The Shattered Meridian is an archipelago civilization whose survival depends on maps. Most inner routes are well known, but outer charts disagree, old observatories stand on remote islands, drowned roads appear at extreme tides, and some navigation markers predate every living culture. The world rewards exploration, evidence and careful inference rather than effortless magic.
locations: Meridian Harbor, Deniz's known home port
Beacon Ridge, a chain of signal towers above the inner strait
the Drowned Causeway, visible only during rare low tides
the Outer Mist Line, where official charts become incomplete
an abandoned tide observatory on a distant mapped island
social_context: cartographers and navigators hold respected public roles
island councils depend on reliable sea routes
young apprentices may take meaningful expedition roles within established safety rules
merchant captains, fishers and scholars often disagree about what counts as trustworthy evidence
old folklore sometimes preserves real geographic information in distorted form
known_pressures: several navigation beacons no longer agree with official charts
outer-island routes are becoming economically important
storm season will eventually restrict long voyages
different groups have reasons to prefer different versions of the map
known_world_facts: Meridian Harbor is Deniz's home port and training base.
Beacon Ridge is part of the known inner navigation network.
The Drowned Causeway is known to appear only during rare low tides.
The Outer Mist Line marks the edge of reliable official charts.
An abandoned tide observatory exists on a distant mapped island.
Several beacon readings have recently become difficult to reconcile with official charts, but no accepted explanation exists yet.

main_saga_public.title: The Uncharted Disagreement
main_saga_public.goal: Discover why the Shattered Meridian's ancient navigation infrastructure and living tides no longer agree with official charts.
main_saga_public.stakes: Outer routes vital to island trade may become unsafe or unusable if the true cause of the discrepancies goes unaddressed.
main_saga_public.central_mystery: Something in the deep channels or the ancient beacon-markers is behaving in ways no known chart-making era can explain.

eligible_main_saga_milestones.summary: Deniz notices a beacon reading that disagrees with the official chart by a margin too large for instrument error.
eligible_main_saga_milestones.state_condition: Deniz has one documented anomaly and a working hypothesis that it is not simple mistake.
consequence_options: The friend becomes curious and offers to help verify.

active_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's practical-minded friend may want to pursue independent proof through experiments rather than surveying, creating friendly rivalry.
active_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Provides low-stakes roleplay and callback material outside the Main Saga.

creation_constraints: New entities must fit low-magic, rule-bound tidal/magnetic world logic.
New NPCs should have plausible reasons to intersect Deniz's apprentice life.
Do not contradict established hidden truths.

candidates.title: The Ridge That Disagrees
candidates.differentiation_key: instrument-based anomaly under institutional time pressure at Beacon Ridge
candidates.logline: During a routine calibration check, Deniz finds a beacon reading that refuses to match the official chart — and has only until the next scheduled maintenance to prove it isn't just instrument error.
candidates.protagonist_role: Apprentice surveyor assigned limited, supervised access to verify beacon instrument readings at Beacon Ridge.
candidates.immediate_objective: Gather a second, defensible reading confirming the beacon's magnetic drift before the mentor's review deadline or scheduled beacon maintenance erases the chance to check again.
candidates.inciting_event: While logging a routine calibration, Deniz notices the beacon's reading has drifted from the official chart by a margin too large to blame on instrument tolerance, and a hurried second check seems to confirm it.
candidates.central_problem: The drift could be a broken instrument, an outdated chart, or something in the beacon stone itself — each explanation demands different next steps, and Deniz has too little time and too little authority to test all three properly.
candidates.wonder_or_discovery: Close inspection reveals the beacon's old markings carry a faint, regular patterning that doesn't match any survey era Deniz has been taught, hinting the structure may be older than anyone assumes.
candidates.stakes: Report too early with thin evidence and the mentor may dismiss the anomaly and restrict Deniz's fieldwork; wait too long and scheduled maintenance may reset the beacon before the drift can be confirmed at all.
constraints: Limited and intermittently supervised access to the instruments
A hard deadline before scheduled beacon maintenance
Must not disturb or recalibrate official equipment without permission
Only one set of reliable field tools available
candidates.meaningful_choice_pressure: Deniz must decide whether to bring the mentor a single striking but unconfirmed reading now to secure continued access, or risk losing the beacon entirely by waiting for a second confirming measurement.
candidates.mystery_or_forward_question: Whether the drift comes from instrument error, an outdated chart, or something active in the old stone remains unresolved, though one hypothesis becomes newly credible.
candidates.local_payoff: The mentor agrees the anomaly is worth formally logging rather than dismissing, and Deniz earns a small but real expansion of independent fieldwork trust.
persistent_outcomes_possible: A documented, dated anomaly log tied to the beacon
A shift in the mentor's assessment of Deniz's methodology
Possible continued or expanded access to Beacon Ridge instruments
A rumor among fellow apprentices about the disagreeing beacon

candidates.title: The Narrow Window
candidates.differentiation_key: friend rivalry over competing methods against a hard tidal deadline at the Drowned Causeway
candidates.logline: When the rare low tide finally exposes the Drowned Causeway, Deniz and a practical-minded friend disagree over how to prove anything about it before the sea reclaims their only chance.
candidates.protagonist_role: Apprentice surveyor accompanying a friend to document a rare, short-lived exposure of the Drowned Causeway.
candidates.immediate_objective: Record usable evidence of the causeway's carved markers before the tide returns and buries them again.
candidates.inciting_event: Deniz and the friend reach the exposed causeway only to realize the tide window is shorter than expected, and they immediately clash over Deniz's careful survey approach versus the friend's faster hands-on testing.
candidates.central_problem: Two different methods compete for the same limited time: slow, careful documentation risks running out of tide before finishing, while fast experimentation risks damaging fragile markings or missing subtle details — and the carved symbols themselves seem oddly directional, possibly shifted or altered.
candidates.wonder_or_discovery: The causeway markers include carved directional symbols pointing outward toward the Outer Mist Line, faintly echoing a pattern Deniz has half-noticed before but never placed.
candidates.stakes: If the tide window is wasted through disagreement or rushed methods, they lose the only clear evidence for possibly years; if they misrepresent the find later, it could damage both their credibility with the harbor council.
constraints: An unpredictable, short low-tide window
Unstable, slippery causeway surface
No adult supervision present to arbitrate decisions
Only hand tools and sketch materials available on site
candidates.meaningful_choice_pressure: Deniz must decide whether to slow down and merge both methods for stronger but partial evidence, or split up with the friend to cover more ground quickly at the risk of weaker, harder-to-defend results.
candidates.mystery_or_forward_question: Whether the causeway symbols connect to the beacon disagreements elsewhere in the strait remains an open question beyond this episode.
candidates.local_payoff: The pair manage to secure one solid, well-documented rubbing or sketch of the symbol before the tide returns, and settle — for now — how they'll work together on future finds.
persistent_outcomes_possible: A shift in the friend rivalry dynamic toward cooperation or competition
A documented rubbing or sketch of the causeway symbol
Changed location-state knowledge of the Drowned Causeway
A new rumor linking the causeway to wider navigation disagreements
world_specific_elements: Outer Mist Line as a directional reference

candidates.title: Someone Else's Notes
candidates.differentiation_key: self-contained exploration mystery of an abandoned observatory with a competing-interest wrinkle, independent of the beacon-drift thread
candidates.logline: Sent to catalog a supposedly abandoned tide observatory before the council decides its fate, Deniz finds instruments that shouldn't still work and notes in a hand that isn't anyone's on record.
candidates.protagonist_role: Apprentice given rare permission to help catalog a distant island's abandoned tide observatory ahead of a council decision on its future.
candidates.immediate_objective: Assess and document which instruments and logbooks are worth preserving before the council's fixed decision deadline.
candidates.inciting_event: On arrival, Deniz finds the observatory isn't as untouched as expected — some instruments are still calibrated, and a logbook contains recent-looking entries in an unfamiliar hand.
candidates.central_problem: With only a short visit window before the ship departs, Deniz must figure out what's genuinely valuable to report while also piecing together who has been visiting the supposedly abandoned site and why, without enough time or authority to fully investigate either.
candidates.wonder_or_discovery: An intact mechanical tide-instrument of an older design, paired with coded shorthand notes that partially resemble known conventions but seem to predate them.
candidates.stakes: The report Deniz brings back could tip the council toward preserving the observatory or scrapping it, and misjudging the mystery visitor could either miss a valuable ally or trigger unnecessary alarm.
constraints: A short visit window tied to the ship's departure
Fragile, easily damaged old equipment
Authority only to recommend, not decide
Uncertainty about who else currently has access to the site
candidates.meaningful_choice_pressure: Deniz must decide whether to report the evidence of a recent visitor immediately, risking a premature council reaction that could close off further investigation, or quietly gather more information first, risking being seen as withholding something important.
candidates.mystery_or_forward_question: Who has been visiting the observatory, and why, remains unresolved and open for future exploration.
candidates.local_payoff: Deniz returns with a persuasive, well-documented case for at least partial preservation of the observatory, anchored by a genuine and impressive discovery.
persistent_outcomes_possible: Changed location-state for the observatory (flagged for preservation or further study)
A new item: the recovered instrument or a copy of the coded notes
A new rumor about a mystery visitor
Improved standing with the island council
A new eligible thread about who else uses the observatory
